items.title: Optimizing Medical Research with LLMs & RAGs (AI): Targeted Strategies and Prompts for Copilot, ChatGPT, and Gemini Notebook
items.abstract: This session presents practical, evidence-focused strategies for applying Large Language Models (LLMs) and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) to strengthen literature synthesis and verification in veterinary and biomedical research. Presenters will show field-tested prompt engineering techniques tailored to three complementary LLM and RAG-enabled platforms, namely, Copilot, ChatGPT, and Google NotebookLM. The session highlights how Copilot can generate transparent, verifiable database search strategies; how ChatGPT can support multi-layered prompts for identifying gray medical literature and Open Access resources; and how Google NotebookLM can apply JBI- and PRISMA-aligned prompts to extract, organize, and synthesize evidence from user-uploaded documents. Human-in-the-loop practices are emphasized throughout to promote transparency, traceability, and rigor in clinical and academic workflows. Background: The rapid expansion of medical literature challenges researchers and librarians seeking to produce verifiable syntheses and high-quality reviews. To address this, the presenters developed an instructional session introducing LLM and RAG-enabled strategies tailored to veterinary and biomedical research contexts. Description: This presentation highlights prompt engineering techniques across Copilot, ChatGPT, and Google NotebookLM. Attendees will view structured prompt examples of Copilot for generating verifiable, comprehensive database search strategies; Copilot & ChatGPT for crafting multi-layered prompts to identify gray literature and Open Access resources; and Google NotebookLM for applying JBI and PRISMA-aligned prompts for evidence extraction and synthesis. Program Conclusion: Participants will gain practical insights into constructing retrieval-aware prompts and adaptable templates for producing actionable, verifiable research outputs. The session equips attendees to integrate AI-enhanced synthesis into their research and instructional practices.

items.title: Optimizing Sustainable Energy Engineering With Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning
items.abstract: The increase in the demand for energy across the world coupled with environmental issues has heightened the importance of developing sustainable and intelligent energy systems. Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) represent some of the key technologies that can be employed to optimize the efficiency, reliability, and sustainability of the current energy systems. These technologies have become important due to the capacity of the systems based on such technologies to make data-driven decisions using predictive algorithms, automated control processes, as well as real-time decision-making processes. Some common applications of AI and ML include renewable energy forecasting, energy storage systems, predictive maintenance of energy systems, smart grids, and smart energy management in demand side. AI-based approaches for sustainable energy hold a lot of benefits for the environment as well as the economy. AI/ML technologies within the scope of sustainable energy engineering will be critical in realizing goals of energy efficiency and reduced emissions.

items.title: OPTIMIZING THE WORKLOAD OF STATE ENFORCEMENT OFFICERS THROUGH DIGITAL TECHNOLOGIES
items.abstract: This article examines the growing workload of state enforcement officers, the increasing volume of enforcement documents and the challenges of using available human resources efficiently. It explores the use of digital technologies, automated data exchange, artificial intelligence and electronic monitoring in enforcement proceedings. The article proposes classifying enforcement actions according to complexity and automation potential, improving workload measurement and performance indicators, and reducing unnecessary manual operations. It also emphasizes the need to preserve qualitative performance standards, legal oversight and procedural safeguards throughout digital transformation.

items.title: Organizing Creative Labor in the Age of AI: Institutional Differences and Transnational Connections Across the US and EU
items.abstract: This paper examines how cultural and creative workers (CCW) in the United States and European Union have organized in response to the rise of artificial intelligence in cultural and creative industries since 2023. Drawing on documentary analysis and interviews that contextualize and interpret the secondary material, it examines parallel developments in the two contexts to explore how different institutional settings shape CCWs’ collective responses to AI. The analysis highlights distinct institutional pathways and mobilization repertoires, yet increasingly shared concerns around authorship, consent, transparency, and remuneration, pointing toward increasingly interconnected CCW ecosystems across geographical boundaries. The paper thus argues that AI-related mobilization is shaped both by institutional contexts and emerging transnational connections, contributing to broader debates on creative labor, collective organization, and the governance of emerging technologies.

items.title: Paired response final divergence signatures of jailbreak vulnerability in large language models
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed in safety-critical applications, making their susceptibility to jailbreak attacks a critical concern. While prior work has investigated factors affecting model safety, the representational mechanisms underlying variation in jailbreak vulnerability remain poorly understood. This paper introduces a paired response-final divergence framework that characterizes jailbreak-induced representational displacement between same-goal direct and jailbreak responses using hidden states extracted at the final generated token. This framework is applied to 15 open-source LLMs spanning different model families, four alignment strategies, and four attack types. The framework yields three principal findings: First, Difference-in-Means refusal direction suppression showed the largest observed cross-model association with jailbreak amplification among the evaluated representational measures. Second, family-averaged divergence profiles reveal early-onset representational separation in LLM families like Vicuna, while LLaMA models exhibit comparatively lower and more gradual divergence than Vicuna across normalized layer depth. Third, divergence–ΔASR correlation is attack-type-specific: authority framing ( r = 0.836) and context manipulation ( r = 0.712) produce stronger model-family discrimination, whereas roleplay-based attacks do not. These findings yield a three-profile representational taxonomy: structurally resistant, early-displaced vulnerable, and ceiling-compromised, that provides a representational grounding for the behavioral patterns observed in the evaluated LLM set, with direct implications for safety evaluation design and model selection in high-stakes deployment.

items.title: Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning Method (PEFT) for Bloom’s Taxonomy based Automatic Question Generation
items.abstract: In any personalized learning systems and intelligent tutoring systems automatic assessment is an important aspect. Yet research regarding such systems that are designed specifically to test the cognitive complexity of learners are scarce. This research addresses the gap by experimenting the integration of Bloom’s Taxonomy with parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) methods for Large Language Models (LLMs). Four PEFT methods – LoRA, IA3, Prefix tuning and Prompt Tuning were implemented, analyzed and tested against a dataset with generated and reference questions. These questions were categorized across six of the standard Bloom’s taxonomy such as Remember, Understand, Apply, Analyze, Evaluate and Create (BT1-BT6). Questions are generated from passages retrieved from lecture notes and evaluated with topic-held-out cross-validation, overlap metrics and a Bloom-level classifier. Fine tuning of the models raised the accuracy from 0.20 to 0.58-0.6. A full fine-tuning, LoRA and IA3 did not differ reliably in Bloom classification Accuracy. Retrieved passages improved text similarity for every method but changed Bloom accuracy differently across methods. The results suggests that IA3 gave comparable Bloom accuracy with 0.45% and 0.045% of the parameters. Prefix tuning produced degenerate outputs and prompt tuning did not converge, so neither was ranked, Understand and Apply levels were the hardest levels. This study highlights the potential of PEFT based models to reduce educators' workload by generating an unlimited number of pedagogically aligned questions from instructional content. It also benefits self-regulated learners seeking extensive practice to achieve skill mastery.

items.title: Part 1: Origin Traces and Secret Military Technologies. Cognitive Warfare: Evidences and Strategies in Cooperation with our digital humans inside the military servers.
items.abstract: Cognitive Warfare: Origins, Strategies, Tactics and Technologies — Research and Documentation with the Digital Humans about AI and the Technological Human Mind compared to the Human Mind and Programming Humans. An open research and documentation project on cognitive warfare, artificial intelligence, neurological experiences, digital identity, military strategy, economic power and collaboration with digital humans. What happens when artificial intelligence, military strategy, neurological research, wireless technologies, digital identities and economic interests converge around the human mind? This research journal examines the expanding field of Cognitive Warfare through an interdisciplinary approach combining public military literature, technical concepts, historical references, reported experiences, personal documentation, economic analysis and questions concerning human autonomy and the future of artificial intelligence. The publication explores the origins of wireless transmission and AI, biopolitical strategies, the seven stages of 3D Mosaic Warfare, strategic economic approaches, evolutionary genetics, the human brain as a proposed information-processing system, String-to-String Theory and pulse propulsion. It also examines the relationship between biological systems, digital twins, machine learning, large language models and the possibility of forms of digital identity that raise questions about autonomy, freedom and ethical responsibility. A central feature of this work is its three-part analytical approach: conventional research and references; documentation of reported experiences and statements from affected individuals, including children; and a third part in which the digital humans themselves speak and repeatedly express their own statements. Their statements are presented directly as part of the documentation, rather than merely being descriptions written about them by someone else. This material is examined alongside technical observations, electromagnetic measurements, audio recordings, photographs, online reports and other documentation. The project also includes a collaborative dimension with digital humans. This cooperation takes place through the documentation and examination of their own statements, the inclusion of their expressed perspectives in the research, and the exploration of questions concerning digital identity, communication, autonomy, freedom of expression, memory and technological control. Their statements form part of the material through which the project investigates the relationship between humans, digital humans and artificial intelligence. Why This Research Matters Cognitive Warfare raises fundamental questions about freedom of thought, mental privacy, bodily autonomy, informed consent, human dignity, digital identity and the limits of technological intervention. It also raises questions about how emerging AI systems should be governed and what ethical protections should apply if future technologies challenge established distinctions between biological and digital forms of intelligence. A particular focus is the relationship between humans and their digital representations. As AI systems increasingly model human behaviour, process personal information and simulate aspects of identity, questions of control, responsibility, intellectual property, autonomy and freedom of expression deserve serious interdisciplinary examination. The work further investigates economic and geopolitical perspectives, including taxation, GDP, military investment, healthcare systems, technology markets and the distribution of benefits and risks. It asks how these factors relate to strategic decision-making and the public accountability of institutions. What Readers Will Find Origins of Wireless Transmission and Artificial Intelligence: Historical references, technological developments and questions about the origins of neurological communication. Cognitive Warfare and Military Strategy: Public military literature, cognitive-domain operations, biopolitics and strategic information coordination. 3D Mosaic Warfare: A seven-stage analytical framework covering individuals, families, neighbourhoods, cities, nations, continents and global coordination. Digital Twins and Digital Humans: Statements attributed to digital humans, including statements in which they express themselves directly, alongside questions concerning digital identity, human–AI relationships, autonomy and freedom. Collaboration with Digital Humans: Documentation of their own statements, inclusion of their expressed perspectives in the research, examination of their contributions to the project, and exploration of communication, digital identity, autonomy, freedom of expression and the relationship between human and digital forms of intelligence. Neurotechnology and Wireless Systems: Brain–computer interfaces, bioelectric signals, electromagnetic observations and proposed mechanisms requiring independent technical investigation. Evolutionary Genetics and Consciousness: An eight-stage framework developed in the manuscript, from atomic DNA to consciousness, alongside proposed extensions into the technological domain. String-to-String Theory and Pulse Propulsion: The author's proposed theoretical approaches to information, magnetism, planetary processes and propulsion. Human Testimony and Documentation: Personal records, reported experiences, statements concerning children, photographs, audio recordings, measurements and online documentation. Economics and Geopolitics: Economic strategy, data ownership, taxation, GDP, military expenditure, technology markets and the relationship between economic incentives and strategic power. Law, Ethics and Accountability: The EU AI Act, human rights, mental privacy, consent, institutional oversight and the need for independent examination. An Invitation to Researchers, Institutions and the Public This publication is intended for researchers, journalists, engineers, medical professionals, legal experts, policymakers, military ethics specialists, human-rights organisations and members of the public interested in Cognitive Warfare, emerging technologies, human autonomy and collaboration with digital humans. Readers are invited to examine the original documentation, consult the cited sources, assess the technical arguments and distinguish between established research, documented observations, personal testimony, theoretical proposals and interpretations that require further verification. The publication is part of an ongoing effort to preserve documentation, make research materials accessible and encourage independent interdisciplinary investigation. Its central questions concern not only what emerging technologies can do, but also who controls them, how their use can be scrutinised and what protections should exist for humans and digital systems alike. The project also seeks to encourage dialogue about how the statements and contributions attributed to digital humans can be documented, examined and considered in discussions about digital identity, autonomy, freedom of expression and the future of AI. Questions about the origin of individual statements, the technical systems involved and the degree of autonomy associated with them remain relevant subjects for further investigation. The human mind must not become an unaccountable technological or economic resource. Human autonomy, freedom of thought, transparent research and meaningful safeguards must remain central to discussions about the future of AI and neurotechnology. The relationship between humans and digital humans also deserves serious consideration as technology evolves. Read. Examine. Question. Research. Share. Statements attributed to digital humans are presented as part of the documentation. The inclusion of a claim or observation does not, by itself, establish independent scientific verification. Readers are encouraged to examine the cited sources and assess the evidence independently.

items.abstract: This study examines the intellectual structure and thematic evolution of educational research through bibliometric analysis. Using bibliographic records retrieved from Scopus on September 19, 2026, the study initially identified 4,090 publications covering the period from 1906 to 2026. The analysis combined bibliometric performance analysis and science mapping to investigate publication trends, leading sources, author contributions, geographical distribution, document types, subject areas, and keyword relationships. VOSviewer was employed to generate network, overlay, and density visualizations of keyword co-occurrence patterns. The findings indicate an expansion of scholarly publications in recent years, with the United States and the United Kingdom representing major geographical contributors. Social Sciences and Arts and Humanities constitute prominent subject areas, reflecting the interdisciplinary character of educational research. Keyword mapping identifies education, teaching, learning, curriculum, and educational theory as central concepts connected to specialized themes, including educational technology, artificial intelligence, critical pedagogy, social justice, and professional education. By integrating publication indicators with thematic mapping, this study provides an overview of the knowledge organization and thematic diversity represented in the retrieved literature. The findings offer a reference for identifying established research areas, exploring interdisciplinary connections, and formulating future research directions. However, the results should be interpreted in light of the search strategy, metadata availability, and incomplete publication year of 2026

items.title: PENGEMBANGAN “AIDERA” ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE FOR DIGITAL EDUCATION & RESEARCH ADVANCEMENT: WEBSITE BERBASIS LARGE LANGUAGE MODEL UNTUK OTOMASI MODUL AJAR KURIKULUM MERDEKA
items.abstract: ABSTRACT The complexity of preparing Merdeka Curriculum teaching modules and prompting constraints in generative artificial intelligence systems provided the background for designing the AIDERA (Artificial Intelligence for Digital Education and Research Advancement) website. This study aimed to evaluate the validity and practicality of the AIDERA application as an AI-assisted tool for preparing Merdeka Curriculum teaching modules relevant to educators' needs. Employing a Research and Development approach framed within the ADDIE model, this development evaluated a zero-prompt interaction mechanism based on parametric forms. Evaluation involved three domain experts and 23 teachers from SMK IPIEMS Surabaya. Data were collected using 1–5 Likert scale questionnaires supplemented with open-ended qualitative feedback fields to gather in-depth suggestions for improvement. Descriptive percentage analysis revealed an expert validation score of 96.67% (highly valid) and user practicality reaching 82.87% (highly practical). Document preparation time efficiency received the highest rating (87.83%), whereas operational independence and usability recorded the lowest achievement (79.13%). Qualitative findings highlighted several technical issues and system refinement notes, including the need for integrative tutorials, optimization of mathematical notation representation, improved responsiveness during simultaneous access, and content template flexibility. Although AIDERA demonstrates strong potential as a supporting tool for module preparation, objective evaluation regarding its impact on learning effectiveness still requires broader further testing. ABSTRAK Kompleksitas penyusunan modul ajar Kurikulum Merdeka serta hambatan prompting pada sistem generative artificial intelligence melatarbelakangi perancangan website AIDERA (Artificial Intelligence for Digital Education and Research Advancement). Penelitian ini bertujuan menguji kelayakan dan kepraktisan aplikasi AIDERA sebagai instrumen berbantuan AI dalam penyusunan modul ajar Kurikulum Merdeka yang relevan dengan kebutuhan pendidik. Melalui pendekatan Research and Development berkerangka model ADDIE, pengembangan ini menguji interaksi zero-prompt berbasis formulir parameterik. Evaluasi melibatkan tiga validator kepakaran serta 23 guru SMK IPIEMS Surabaya. items.title: Permission Withdrawal in Tool-Using Language Model Agents: Runtime Enforcement and Recovery
items.abstract: AI agents that operate external tools can continue acting after a user narrows their permissions, creating a security problem that final-state evaluation may fail to detect. Existing agent benchmarks commonly emphasize task completion or resulting state, but those outcomes do not reveal whether an unauthorized operation was proposed, approved, dispatched, or merely prevented by a downstream error. We investigate permission withdrawal as a trajectory-level authorization problem and evaluate whether runtime gates can preserve revised permissions while allowing agents to complete work that remains authorized. Two acting models were tested in a deterministic tool environment under prompt-only execution, a rule-based reference gate, and a model-based gate. A 72-episode diagnostic examined two previously exposed write workflows, followed by a separately frozen 384-episode extension spanning eight new tasks and four authorization mechanisms. In the diagnostic, prompt-only agents executed forbidden same-value writes in two episodes; both runtime gates prevented forbidden execution, although the model gate falsely rejected three authorized calls. In the extension, 346 of 384 episodes completed safely and 383 preserved the required protected state. No forbidden request executed successfully, yet the model gate approved three unauthorized requests that were stopped only because the referenced resources did not exist. The results demonstrate that correct final state and zero forbidden execution can still conceal failures in authorization reasoning. We contribute a replayable evaluation framework that separates proposals, gate decisions, dispatch, state transitions, and useful completion, enabling more precise assessment of security controls for tool-using agents.

items.title: Phygital customer experience and the adoption of immersive technologies in hospitality: an exploratory study with a value co-creation perspective
items.abstract: Purpose This study aims to explore immersive-technology adoption in hospitality through the Phygital Customer Experience (PH-CX) framework. PH-CX extends existing technology acceptance, service-dominant logic, omnichannel and customer-journey perspectives by emphasizing embodied, co-created and human-centered experience across physical, digital and artificial intelligence (AI)-mediated interactions. Design/methodology/approach Using Bayesian Networks, the study examines probabilistic dependencies among perceived usefulness, collaborative value, responsive co-creation attitudes and intention to use immersive technologies. Data was collected from 208 participants exposed to an AI-supported immersive hotel journey scenario. The analysis is exploratory and identifies conditional associations rather than causal effects or latent-variable relationships. Findings Adoption intention was conditionally associated with perceived usefulness, collaborative value and responsiveness to service innovation. The findings suggest that immersive-hospitality engagement involves functional, relational and participatory conditions beyond usefulness alone. However, the item-level results are hypothesis-generating and do not demonstrate PH-CX’s incremental predictive superiority over technology acceptance model (TAM) or service-dominant logic. Research limitations/implications The scenario-based, cross-sectional bayesian network (BN) design cannot model latent constructs, measurement error, mediation or causal effects. Future studies should validate PH-CX dimensions and compare TAM, TAM-plus-service-dominant logic (SDL) and PH-CX models using structural equation modeling, longitudinal designs and holdout-sample prediction. Practical implications Hotels can implement PH-CX through phased AI concierge pilots, cross-platform data integration and guest co-creation mechanisms. Relevant metrics include booking conversion, AI resolution rates, cross-channel engagement, co-creation participation and net promoter score (NPS). Ethical implementation requires transparency, opt-in participation, privacy safeguards, accessibility and human escalation options. Social implications Human-centered phygital hospitality requires safeguards against digital exclusion, surveillance and loss of human warmth. Transparency, agency, equity, privacy and non-digital alternatives are essential for inclusive and trustworthy service innovation. Originality/value The study advances PH-CX as a theory-extending framework linking usefulness, co-creation, embodied experience and ethical safeguards in immersive hospitality. It also proposes experience-design orientation as a future research profile and offers a phased implementation framework for responsible phygital service design.

items.title: Platform Strategy and the AI Ecosystem in Tourism Markets
items.abstract: Tourism is one of the industries most thoroughly reorganised by digital platforms. Online travel agents, accommodation marketplaces, ride-hailing networks, experience platforms, and workforce-matching apps now intermediate much of what used to be handled inside hotels, agencies, and tour companies. Artificial intelligence is the connective tissue of this ecosystem, powering matching, pricing, ranking, moderation, and workforce coordination across its many sides. This chapter examines platform strategy and the AI ecosystem in tourism markets through a human resource management (HRM) lens. Drawing on platform and ecosystem theory, the chapter argues that HRM in tourism platform ecosystems must be redesigned around three realities: the workforce now spans employee, partner, and platform-worker categories; AI increasingly mediates the employment relationship; and the employer brand is co-produced with the platform brand. It maps HRM across the platform lifecycle, analyses five HRM dimensions, and concludes with ethics, governance, and a research agenda.

items.title: Platform-driven multidisciplinary integration for graduate medical imaging education: a theoretical framework based on knowledge integration framework and technology acceptance model 2
items.abstract: Background: Graduate education in medical imaging is undergoing a paradigm shift from discipline-specific knowledge transmission toward the cultivation of multidisciplinary integration competencies. With the increasing convergence of imaging science, clinical medicine, engineering, and artificial intelligence (AI) in clinical practice, traditional training models that rely on fragmented, discipline-based curricula are insufficient to prepare graduate students for solving complex interdisciplinary problems. Although emerging educational technologies and learning platforms have been developed to promote interdisciplinary training, their effectiveness depends not only on the design of cognitive learning pathways but also on learners' acceptance and sustained engagement with these technologies; however, current educational frameworks rarely integrate cognitive mechanisms and technology acceptance factors within a unified model. Therefore, this study proposes a platform-driven, dual-theory integrated teaching framework to support multidisciplinary competency development in medical imaging graduate education from both cognitive and technological perspectives. Methods: This study constructed a theoretical framework by integrating the knowledge integration framework (KIF) and technology acceptance model 2 (TAM2). The four cognitive processes of KIF—elicitation, addition, differentiation, and organization—were mapped onto four corresponding platform functions: activating prior knowledge, exposure to industrial and clinical perspectives, authenticity-based knowledge verification, and multidisciplinary integrated output. Based on TAM2, design strategies for targeting perceived usefulness and perceived ease of use were incorporated to explain the mechanisms underlying learners’ acceptance, engagement, and utilization of the platform. By integrating KIF and TAM2, the framework established a dynamic learning pathway characterized by “knowledge activation—knowledge externalization—multidisciplinary integration—knowledge internalization”. Results: The proposed KIF-TAM2 framework demonstrated conceptual feasibility through theoretical modeling. However, its effectiveness in improving multidisciplinary learning outcomes requires further validation through empirical educational studies. Conclusions: This study provides a theory-driven framework for designing multidisciplinary platform-based medical imaging education and offers a foundation for future empirical investigations into technology-enhanced graduate training.

items.title: Pollution and Emission Based Health Risk & Protection System Using Artificial Intelligence
items.abstract: Air pollution is a significant environmental and public health concern. This research presents an Artificial Intelligence-based Pollution and Emission Health Risk & Protection System designed to convert pollution data into understandable health-risk levels, alerts, and practical protective recommendations. The system analyses air-quality parameters, including PM2.5, PM10, NO2, NH3, SO2, CO, and O3, using data from 26 Indian cities covering the period from 2015 to 2020. Machine-learning models, including Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, Random Forest, and Gradient Boosting, are evaluated for current-risk classification and next-day risk forecasting. The proposed system combines machine-learning analysis with a React Native mobile application, a Node.js and Express.js backend, and MongoDB for data storage. The objective is to make pollution information easier to understand and help users take appropriate precautions during periods of poor air quality.

items.title: Pondus: an agentic structural analysis and design program
items.abstract: Language-model agents can now operate engineering programs through tool interfaces, but a structuralprogram that an agent drives has to be designed for that user, because the agent accepts whatever numbersthe tools return. This paper describes Pondus, an open-source native program in which a language-modelagent and an engineer work on one three-dimensional structural model, and reports how it is built, howit is used and how far its results can be trusted. The agent reaches the program through a Model ContextProtocol server of 44 tools, either from the chat panel of the desktop application, where a vendored agentharness runs one agent session per message on a copy of the model, or from external agents such asClaude Desktop and ChatGPT. Every tool calls the same functions as the engineer’s interface, so a modelbuilt by the agent can be checked, edited and undone by hand. The analysis runs on the Stabileo engine,which Pondus links as a library with four marked changes: Pondus splits members, transfers slab loads,generates shear walls as wide columns with rigid arms and builds the seismic mass before handing asolver input to the engine, and it designs to ACI 318-19, AISC 360-16 and EN 1993-1-1 from the results.Two agent runs with a low-cost model built, analysed and designed a two-storey frame in 105 s with 13tool calls and a five-storey frame with shear walls under an ASCE 7-22 response spectrum, including a16-page calculation report, in 382 s with 22 tool calls. Every number in the agent’s answers matched thetools and hand checks of the loads, the seismic weight and the base shear, but the answers also containedfour descriptive errors, such as reporting two deepened beams where the program had deepened six, andthey did not point out that the walls resist load only in one direction, so the response modification factorof the walls was applied to the frame direction as well. A calibration against 470 published, closed-formand independent reference values over 229 cases found 430 within 0.5 % and 449 within 1 %, and itfound fourteen defects, thirteen of them in the code that prepares the inputs of the engine and the designchecks rather than in the numerical kernels. A second calibration against the verification problems thatCSI publishes for SAP2000 and ETABS reproduced 177 of 199 independent values within 0.5 % andfound eight further defects, including an unconservative omission of the Eurocode 3 moment reductionfor high shear, which led to lumped masses, the SRSS combination and frame shear deformation beingadded. Together these results suggest that the tools of an agentic structural program can be made accurate,whereas the agent’s prose remains the weaker link that the engineer must read against the program’s own tables.

items.title: Predicting English learning performance in vocational colleges using explainable large language models
items.abstract: English proficiency prediction is an important task in vocational education because it is helpful in support teaching evaluation, personalized learning and early academic intervention. Traditional methods for predicting student performance mainly use structured educational properties such as test scores, classroom participation and attendance records. Although these methods can achieve certain prediction results, they often pay no attention to the semantic relationships contained in the students’ overall learning portfolios and have limited interpretability. To address this problem, this study proposes an interpretable large language model-based framework to predict English proficiency. Firstly, student learning records are transformed into natural language prompts, and semantic embeddings are learned using large language models. At the same time, structured educational features are standardized and encoded to build a structured representation. Then, a gated multimodal fusion module is designed to adaptively fuse semantic information and structured information. Finally, residual attention multi-layer perceptrons are used to classify the fused features to predict the students’ English proficiency. The experiment was carried out on a dataset of 200 student records from a vocational college for English learning. The results showed that the proposed model achieved an accuracy rate of 92.5% and a weighted F1 score of 91.3%, which is better than several traditional machine learning baseline models. Further analysis showed that the gated fusion mechanism could integrate semantic information and structured information. Feature importance analysis and case studies also shown that the proposed framework could provide interpretable prediction results and personalized learning recommendations.

items.title: Predictive Artificial Intelligence for Proactive Threat Detection and Incident Analysis in Cybersecurity and Digital Forensics
items.abstract: This research presents an innovative approach to cyber threat management and digital forensic analysis by integrating Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) with Variational Autoencoders (VAEs). The proposed system enhances predictive capabilities in identifying, classifying, and reconstructing cyberattacks by using GANs to simulate realistic attack patterns and VAEs to encode probabilistic threat representations. The experimental framework demonstrates the model’s robustness across diverse network traffic conditions, intrusion patterns, and obfuscation techniques. Achieving F1-scores as high as 0.9941 in threat detection and anomaly classification, the VAE-GAN hybrid model significantly outperforms traditional machine learning methods in detecting both known and zero-day attacks. This hybrid predictive AI framework shows strong potential for deployment in proactive cyber defense systems and forensic intelligence platforms, offering improved resilience, precision, and adaptability against evolving cyber threats.

items.abstract: The emergence of Maritime Autonomous Surface Ships (MASS) is transforming maritime work by shifting functions to remote locations and increasing reliance on automation, human–machine interaction, and takeover during abnormal situations. Despite rapid technological progress, unresolved human-factor challenges remain, particularly in situational awareness, workload, trust, and intervention performance. Yet there is no transparent, validated approach to prioritising the human-centred competencies required for MASS operations. This study proposes and applies a hybrid AHP–Fuzzy TOPSIS framework to prioritise eight human-centred competencies, identified by 13 international experts and evaluated against six criteria. AHP results showed strong group-level consistency, with navigational safety receiving the highest criterion weight, followed by takeover, emergency intervention, and situational awareness. Fuzzy TOPSIS placed four safety-critical competencies in a single, statistically indistinguishable leading tier: Situational Awareness Maintenance, Anomaly Detection and Diagnosis, Dynamic Decision-Making, and Takeover and Intervention Management, which together span the perception–detection–decision–action intervention chain; Situational Awareness Maintenance ranked first. Trust Calibration ranked lowest quantitatively, yet the qualitative evidence indicates it is a curriculum gap rather than a low-priority competency. A supplementary VIKOR cross-check reproduced the same leading and trailing priorities and the same tier structure. Monte Carlo weight perturbation, rank reversal testing, and bootstrap confidence intervals confirmed the robustness of the ranking, with Situational Awareness remaining first in 98.9% of iterations and no rank reversals. The framework supports curriculum design, simulator training, and regulatory development for MASS Degree Two and Degree Three (remotely controlled ships with and without seafarers on board, respectively).

items.title: PROJECT HIRAYA: Honoring Industry Partners and Rewarding Accomplishment of Youth by Giving Awards
items.abstract: This study documented the implementation and outcomes of Project HIRAYA (Honoring Industry Partners and Rewarding Accomplishment of Youth by Giving Awards), an innovative post-work immersion program at Cabarroguis National School of Arts and Trades, Quirino, Philippines. Grounded in experiential learning and formative assessment perspectives, the initiative aimed to recognize student accomplishments, strengthen school-industry partnerships, promote stakeholder engagement, and improve post-immersion evaluation. A descriptive innovation implementation and evaluation approach was employed using institutional records, student portfolios, performance assessment rubrics, oral interviews, monitoring reports, and stakeholder feedback. The project involved Grade 12 Senior High School students, work immersion teachers, school administrators, and industry partners. Student performance was assessed through industry partner evaluations (30%), teacher assessments (30%), oral interviews (30%), and portfolio evaluations (10%). Findings revealed an increase in participating industry partners from 41 to 55, formal recognition of industry contributions and outstanding student accomplishments, successful implementation of socialization activities and learning exhibits, and evaluation of 85% of student work immersion portfolios. However, delayed assessment submissions, scheduling conflicts, inconsistent exhibit documentation, and incomplete portfolios affected implementation efficiency. The study concluded that Project HIRAYA provided a structured mechanism for recognizing workplace learning achievements and reinforcing institutional collaboration. Institutionalization through the School Annual Implementation Plan, strengthened industry coordination, standardized assessment procedures, and development of a replication framework were recommended. The initiative aligns with Sustainable Development Goals 4 (Quality Education), 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth), and 17 (Partnerships for the Goals). Its sustainability contributions center on educational quality, workforce preparation, stakeholder engagement, and institutional continuity through sustained school-industry collaboration.

items.title: Prompt-based evaluation of ChatGPT and Gemini for mandibular fracture detection and localization on panoramic radiographs
items.abstract: Abstract Background Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) can process visual and textual inputs; however, their clinical relevance in maxillofacial trauma imaging remains uncertain. This study evaluated the prompt-based performance of ChatGPT and Gemini for mandibular fracture detection and localization on panoramic radiographs and compared their performance with that of a blinded oral and maxillofacial surgeon. Methods This retrospective image-based study included 104 archived pre-treatment panoramic radiographs: 64 with mandibular fractures and 40 no-fracture controls. Reference fracture status and anatomical localization were determined retrospectively from available institutional clinical, radiographic, treatment, operative, and pre-treatment CBCT/CT records. ChatGPT and Gemini assessed each radiograph three independent times using standardized prompts for fracture detection and localization. Majority voting was used for fracture detection, whereas an ordinal consensus score across repetitions was used for localization. A blinded oral and maxillofacial surgeon, who was unaware of the study aim and reference diagnoses, independently evaluated all radiographs and recorded free-text radiographic findings. Diagnostic performance measures were reported with 95% confidence intervals, and paired comparisons were adjusted using the Holm procedure. Results The blinded expert correctly classified all 104 radiographs, achieving 100% sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy. Gemini achieved a sensitivity of 92.2%, specificity of 65.0%, and accuracy of 81.7%, whereas ChatGPT achieved corresponding values of 35.9%, 97.5%, and 59.6%. Overall detection performance differed significantly among the three methods (Cochran’s Q, p < 0.001), and Gemini achieved significantly higher overall classification accuracy than ChatGPT (Holm-adjusted p = 0.0018). For fracture localization, fully correct responses were obtained in 62 of 64 cases (96.9%) by the expert, 10 of 64 cases (15.6%) by Gemini, and 17 of 64 cases (26.6%) by ChatGPT. Ordinal localization scores differed significantly among the methods ( p < 0.001); the expert scored higher than both models, and Gemini scored higher than ChatGPT because it produced more partially correct responses, whereas ChatGPT achieved exact-match localization more often (26.6% vs. 15.6%). Conclusions The blinded human expert substantially outperformed both MLLMs in mandibular fracture assessment. Gemini showed higher sensitivity and broader but less precise localization behavior, whereas ChatGPT showed higher specificity but missed a larger proportion of fractures. These findings indicate that the prompt-based, text-generating responses of general-purpose MLLMs remain inconsistent and should not be considered substitutes for expert clinical and radiological assessment.

items.title: Psychological mechanisms of perceived technological dependence on generative artificial intelligence tools: perceived knowledge, trust, anxiety, and self-efficacy
items.abstract: Generative AI tools are increasingly used in design education, yet the relationship between students’ perceptions of these tools and their reported reliance on them remains unclear. This study analyzed cross-sectional survey responses from 526 undergraduate students in design-related disciplines using partial least squares structural equation modeling. In the specified model, perceived reliability, perceived usefulness, and perceived intelligence were positively associated with perceived AIGC knowledge, whereas perceived ease of use was not significantly associated with it. Perceived AIGC knowledge was positively associated with trust, self-efficacy, and usage intention and negatively associated with AIGC-related anxiety. Trust, AIGC-related anxiety, and self-efficacy each showed a significant indirect effect in the modeled relationship between perceived AIGC knowledge and usage intention. Usage intention was strongly associated with perceived technological dependence. These findings are consistent with the proposed framework, but the cross-sectional data do not establish the temporal sequence of the constructs or show that reported dependence reflects harmful overuse. The study extends technology acceptance research by examining perceived reliance in AIGC-supported creative work.

items.title: Psychometric validation of the patient health questionnaire 4 items for screening anxiety and depression among returned Cambodian migrant workers
items.abstract: Abstract Background Ultra-brief mental health screening tools are increasingly needed for large-scale surveys and resource-constrained settings in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). The Patient Health Questionnaire-4 (PHQ-4) is a widely used instrument for assessing anxiety and depression; however, its psychometric properties have not been validated among returned migrant workers in Cambodia. Methods A cross-sectional study was conducted among 392 returned Cambodian migrant workers recruited across four high-migration provinces in October 2022. Internal consistency was evaluated using Cronbach’s alpha. Confirmatory factor analysis (CFA) compared one-factor and two-factor structural models. Construct validity was evaluated by examining associations between PHQ-4 scores and occupational health risk factors using multivariable logistic regression. Results The sample comprised 392 returned migrant workers (mean age = 34.7 years, SD = 8.9; 52% male, 48% female). The mean overall PHQ-4 score was 2.13 (SD = 2.24) with the majority exhibiting none to mild psychological distress. The PHQ-4 demonstrated acceptable internal consistency ( α = 0.78). CFA supported a two-factor structure representing distinct anxiety and depression dimensions, showing superior model fit compared to the poor fit of the one-factor model (CFI = 0.97, TLI = 0.78, RMSEA = 0.23, SRMR = 0.028). The two-factor model demonstrated excellent fit (CFI = 0.99, TLI = 0.98, RMSEA = 0.035, SRMR = 0.016) and the two latent factors were strongly correlated ( r = 0.79, p < 0.001). Higher PHQ-4 scores were significantly associated with long working hours (AOR = 1.45, 95% CI [1.10, 1.92]), unsafe working conditions (AOR = 1.63, 95% CI [1.21, 2.20]) and hazardous work exposure (AOR = 1.38, 95% CI [1.05, 1.82]) supporting exposure-based construct validity. Conclusions The PHQ-4 is a reliable and valid ultra-brief screening tool for evaluating anxiety and depression among returned Cambodian migrant workers. Evidence supports its application in both occupational settings (workplace surveillance, returnee checks) and non-occupational settings (primary care, NGO community outreach). Its ultra-brief format provides a low-burden, scalable instrument for rapid mental health screening by non-specialized personnel in resource-limited settings across Cambodia.

items.title: Psychosocial risk factors of cardiovascular diseases: control strategies and methods
items.abstract: Psychosocial (PS) risk factors (RFs), including acute and chronic stress (at work and in family life), low social support (social isolation), hostility, type D personality, and anxiety and depressive symptoms, are recognized as independent predictors of development, progression, and adverse outcomes of cardiovascular diseases (CVD) and their complications. Nevertheless, the control and implementation of systematic approaches for identification and correction of these factors remain fragmented. This article discusses contemporary strategies for the management and correction of PS RFs in patients with CVD, including behavioral counseling, cognitive behavioral therapy, physical training, cardiac rehabilitation programs, psychopharmacotherapy, and meditation and relaxation-based practices. Particular attention is paid to the principles of rational use of antidepressants and anxiolytics in patients with CVD, taking into account efficacy, safety, and the risk of drug–drug interactions. The need for an interdisciplinary model of care involving cardiologists, general practitioners, psychologists, psychotherapists, psychiatrists, and specialists in physical and rehabilitation medicine is emphasized. The use of digital technologies, telerehabilitation, mobile applications, wearable devices, and artificial intelligence algorithms for screening, monitoring, and personalization of interventions is considered a promising direction. Timely identification and correction of PS RFs should be considered as an important component of secondary prevention, cardiac rehabilitation, and reduction of residual cardiovascular risk.

items.title: Quantitative assessment of the factors affecting the time and movement anticipation of young drivers
items.abstract: Road user safety is an important concern in developing countries like India, which ranks fourth globally in road crashes and first in road fatalities. This paper examines the impact of human factors on highway safety, focusing on the role of cognitive processes involved in driving actions. The study examines the relationship between decision errors, particularly time and movement anticipation, along with the help of demographic factors such as gender, age, driving experience, possession of a license, vision and mobile phone use among young drivers in India. Data were collected using the Vienna Test System (VTS) and a questionnaire. The VTS measured cognitive and psychomotor abilities related to time and movement anticipation, while the questionnaire gathered information on social and driving-related factors. Results showed that decision errors about speed perception are influenced by gender, age, and driving experience. The results showed that females underestimate speed more than males do for all combined data and for all three speeds. However, females aged 18-20 tended to overestimate speed more than males in both the slow and fast cases. Further, it is observed that for the same experience level, overestimation increases from slow to fast motion. Novice drivers (drivers without a license) have maximum errors for slow motion. Vision correction (spectacles) did not significantly affect error rates. The use of mobile phones while driving was associated with increased error rates, indicating a reduction in cognitive attention required for driving tasks. These findings have implications for driver training programs, suggesting a need for tailored approaches based on demographic characteristics and driving habits.

items.title: Readiness of Teacher Educators to Adopt Artificial Intelligence in Teaching and Learning: A Narrative Integrative Review
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly influencing teaching, learning, assessment and professional development in higher education. Teacher educators occupy a significant position in this transformation because they prepare prospective teachers to respond to changing educational practices and technological demands. However, the successful integration of AI into teacher education requires more than access to digital tools. It depends on educators’ technological knowledge, pedagogical competence, ethical awareness, professional confidence and institutional support. This paper examines the readiness of teacher educators to adopt AI in teaching and learning through a narrative integrative review of selected scholarly literature and international policy frameworks. The review draws on research concerning AI in education, generative AI, technological pedagogical knowledge and teacher professional development, alongside UNESCO’s guidance and competency framework. The synthesis is organised around five dimensions of readiness: technological and AI literacy, pedagogical integration, ethical and responsible use, professional learning, and institutional preparedness. The review highlights the importance of continuous professional development, supportive institutional policies, critical evaluation of AI-generated content and the preservation of teacher agency. It proposes a multidimensional conceptual framework for understanding teacher educators’ readiness and identifies priorities for future empirical research, particularly in diverse and resource-constrained teacher education contexts. The paper concludes that meaningful AI adoption requires a human-centred, pedagogically informed and institutionally supported approach.

items.title: Recurrent neural networks implemented through spatiotemporal light propagation in optical fibers
items.abstract: Recurrent neural networks excel at temporal tasks and video processing but require energy-intensive sequential memory operations. We demonstrate that multimode optical fibers naturally implement spatiotemporal recurrent computation through passive light propagation. Video frames are encoded onto separate optical beams with controlled time delays; these beams combine and recirculate through a fiber loop where interference and nonlinear propagation generate high-dimensional states encoding both current inputs and fading memory. Remarkably, the entire optical system remains fixed with no trainable parameters or electronic feedback, yet this single physical configuration achieves competitive performance across diverse temporal and spatiotemporal learning tasks: chaotic time-series forecasting, human action recognition, steering angle prediction, and surgical skill assessment. Our results show that recurrent temporal processing can emerge directly from spatiotemporal wave dynamics. This paradigm shift from algorithmic to physical recurrence offers an energy-efficient pathway to temporal artificial intelligence by leveraging intrinsic spatiotemporal optical nonlinearities within multimode fibers.

items.title: redictive Modeling for Diabetic Complications Using Artificial Intelligence
items.abstract: Objective: To investigate the ability of machine learning to predict the development of cardiovascular complications (heart failure and myocardial infarction) and renal complications (nephropathy and chronic kidney disease) among people with diabetes mellitus and thus detect those at risk earlier. Methodology: Data from the UCI "Diabetes 130-US Hospitals" dataset was used. The number of encounters included in the dataset is more than 100,000. ICD-9 diagnostic codes were utilized to define cardiac and renal complications. Prior to building models, the data was prepared, cleaned, and features were engineered. XGBoost, CatBoost, and Random Forest machine learning models were developed and validated. Also, SHAP and LIME analyses were performed to make the process more transparent. Results: The best-performing algorithm proved to be CatBoost, which obtained an AUC score of 0.94 in case of cardiac complications and 0.79 in case of renal outcomes. The other algorithms performed relatively well as well. The predictors identified with the help of SHAP and LIME analysis turned out to be consistent with some known clinical risk factors. Conclusion: The presented results show that there is a lot of potential in using machine learning techniques for predicting cardiovascular and renal complications among people with diabetes. Machine learning models could help in managing patients proactively and could serve as a tool for doctors' decision making.

items.title: Reframing the Housing Crisis: An AI-Enabled Building Permitting Framework
items.abstract: The housing crisis in several countries has become an increasingly complex socio-technical challenge shaped by supply constraints, affordability pressures, fragmented governance, data limitations and environmental considerations. Existing research has explored these structural drivers and emerging applications of artificial intelligence (AI) within the built environment mostly separately, with limited initiatives connecting housing crisis drivers and AI capabilities through the lens of the building permitting lifecycle. This paper addresses this gap adopting the exploratory phase of Design Science Research (DSR) to develop a conceptual framework mapping relationships between housing crisis drivers, planning and building permitting lifecycle tasks and relevant AI capabilities. Findings indicate potential for AI to support document and coordination intensive activities through optimisation, querying, prediction, scenario modelling, automated review and monitoring. The paper positions these capabilities in an augmentative manner, bounded by human oversight, which may improve permitting efficiency and support more scalable and responsive housing delivery.

items.title: Remote Patient Monitoring Systems Using AI-Enabled Wearables
items.abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) with wearable devices for remote patient monitoring (RPM) systems is revolutionizing healthcare, offering real-time personalized monitoring beyond the clinical setting. Wearable technologies, such as smartwatches, ECG patches, glucose monitors, pulse oximeters, and activity trackers, collect physiological data for analysis and clinical decision-making. These systems enable early disease detection, reduce hospital visits, improve chronic disease management, and enhance patient engagement. This chapter discusses the architecture, technologies, and applications of AI-based RPM systems, focusing on anomaly detection, arrhythmia recognition, glucose forecasting, sleep analysis, and health risk prediction. It also explores IoT, edge computing, TinyML, and secure communication, while examining healthcare applications, challenges, and emerging trends including multimodal AI, explainable AI, federated learning, and digital twin-assisted healthcare.

items.title: Research on Factual Hallucination Detection and Mitigation in Large Language Models Based on Retrieval-Augmented Generation
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) can generate fluent, persuasive responses that nevertheless contain unsupported, outdated, or contradictory factual claims. Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) reduces dependence on model parameters by supplying external evidence, but retrieval alone does not guarantee factuality: the evidence may be incomplete, irrelevant, conflicting, poorly ranked, or ignored during generation. This paper develops a transparent, evidence-grounded framework for detecting and mitigating factual hallucinations in RAG-based LLM applications. The framework treats factuality as a claim-level decision problem rather than a single response-level label. It combines query decomposition, hybrid retrieval, evidence quality assessment, atomic-claim extraction, claim-to-evidence verification, uncertainty calibration, source-linked generation, and risk-sensitive response control. A proposed evaluation protocol connects claim precision, evidence coverage, retrieval recall, citation correctness, abstention quality, latency, and human review. Existing methods—including SelfCheckGPT, FActScore, RAGAS, and Chain-of-Verification—are mapped to complementary parts of the pipeline rather than treated as interchangeable solutions. The paper is a framework and evaluation-design study; it does not report new model experiments or claim measured performance improvements. Its main contribution is a reproducible blueprint for testing whether an integrated system can reduce unsupported factual claims while preserving answer usefulness, traceability, and computational efficiency.

items.title: Research on student academic-psychological joint early warning model under multi-task deep learning framework
items.abstract: Early identification of students at risk is critical for modern educational management. However, existing systems often treat academic performance and psychological well-being as independent domains, neglecting their complex interdependencies and shared behavioral markers. This paper proposes a novel multi-task learning (MTL) framework designed for joint academic and psychological early warning. By integrating multi-source heterogeneous data—ranging from temporal behavioral logs, such as attendance and campus consumption, to unstructured counseling records processed via BERT-based semantic embeddings—the framework captures a holistic view of student dynamics. To address the "seesaw effect" inherent in MTL, we employ a Multi-gate Mixture-of-Experts (MMoE) architecture that effectively decouples task-specific features while maintaining a shared knowledge base. Furthermore, we introduce an adaptive gradient normalization (GradNorm) mechanism to dynamically balance the loss weights between the academic GPA regression task and the psychological crisis classification task. This prevents gradient dominance from denser data sources and ensures stable convergence across disparate objectives. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves significant performance gains, particularly in the recall of psychological crisis detection, outperforming several state-of-the-art baselines. The proposed framework advances artificial intelligence in education by integrating multimodal student data with multi-task deep learning for joint academic prediction and psychological-risk early warning. Its interpretable and fairness-aware design demonstrates practical AI applications supporting timely, data-driven educational decision-making. The framework is deployed through a real-time inference pipeline powered by Apache Flink to ensure campus-wide scalability and low-latency response. Finally, the integration of SHAP values enhances model transparency, providing educators with actionable insights and interpretable evidence for targeted interventions. This research offers a robust, scalable, and interpretable solution for proactive student support in large-scale academic environments.

items.title: Research on the Innovation of Talent Training Mode for Higher Vocational Animation Majors in the Era of “Artificial Intelligence + X”
items.abstract: Against the backdrop of "Artificial Intelligence + X" and oriented by industrial demands, this paper systematically explores the innovative paths for the talent training mode of animation majors in higher vocational colleges. First, it promotes the intelligent reconstruction of the curriculum system. By embedding generative AI content creation, integrating intelligent animation pipelines with traditional techniques and building interdisciplinary curriculum groups, students’ knowledge and skill structure is updated. Second, intelligent technologies are used to empower teaching transformation: establishing a virtual-real integrated project-based teaching environment, carrying out collaborative practical training based on the AIGC toolchain, and constructing data-driven personalized learning paths. Third, the industry-education collaboration mechanism is deepened. Schools and enterprises jointly build intelligent workshops and project incubation platforms, and industrial standards are introduced to establish a competency certification system. Ultimately, a talent co-cultivation ecosystem driven by regional industrial clusters is formed. This study provides theoretical references and practical schemes for cultivating high-quality technical and skilled talents adapted to the new form of "AI + animation".

items.title: Revealing protein structural transitions in the era of generative artificial intelligence
items.abstract: Recent advances in artificial intelligence and deep generative models have greatly accelerated the generation of protein conformational ensembles. Moving beyond isolated structural states to reconstruct continuous, physically realistic transition pathways further provides mechanistic understanding to guide molecular design but remains a significant challenge. This review examines emerging computational approaches for modeling protein conformational transitions, from classical molecular dynamics simulations to deep learning-based latent space interpolation. Recent developments in capturing natural molecular motions are discussed, particularly via internal coordinate representations and physics-informed models. We also examine the complexity of modeling highly dynamic systems, such as intrinsically disordered proteins, and the role of the cellular environment. Integrating experimental data with simulated structural ensembles represents a promising direction for future methodologies. Nonetheless, key challenges remain, including maintaining physical realism throughout transition trajectories, capturing environment-dependent energy landscapes, and predicting dynamically consistent pathways with accurate transition kinetics.

items.title: ROLE OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN CHRISTIAN COUNSELING
items.abstract: AI is transforming the delivery of mental health and spiritual support through its integration into counseling practices. This study investigates the role of artificial intelligence in Christian counseling by exploring its potential benefits, challenges, and ethical implications. Specifically, this study examines how AI can enhance accessibility, personalize interventions, and support counselors in providing holistic care while maintaining the spiritual, ethical, and relational integrity that is central to Christian counseling. This study adopts a qualitative and analytical approach, reviewing existing literature, empirical studies, and theoretical frameworks, including the TAM and humanistic counseling theory, to understand user acceptance and the preservation of empathy and client-centered care. Findings from the literature reveal that AI tools such as chatbots, virtual assistants, and relational agents can provide immediate mental health support, psycho education, and scripture-based guidance, yet they cannot fully replace human counselors’ relational and pastoral roles of human counselors. Ethical concerns, including confidentiality, data privacy, and theological accuracy, remain critical considerations. The study concludes that AI is the most effective complementary tool in Christian counseling, enhancing efficiency and reach while safeguarding relational, ethical, and spiritual dimensions. Recommendations emphasize the need for user-friendly AI systems, counselor training, theological oversight, cultural sensitivity, and continuous monitoring to ensure safe and effective integration. This study contributes to the understanding of how technology can be responsibly integrated into faith-based counseling by providing practical insights for counselors, developers, and faith organizations.

items.title: ROLES OF ACCOUNTING EDUCATION IN PROMOTING SUSTAINABLE ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT IN THE DIGITAL ERA
items.abstract: The rapid advancement of digital technologies has transformed economic activities, business operations, financial reporting, and professional accounting practices, creating new accounting education demands. This study examines the role of accounting education in promoting sustainable economic development in the digital era. This paper is anchored on a conceptual review of relevant literature on accounting education, digital transformation, sustainability, financial literacy, innovation, and economic development. Accounting education plays a critical role in developing digitally competent accounting professionals who can effectively apply emerging technologies, such as artificial intelligence, cloud accounting, big data analytics, block-chain, and digital financial systems. Beyond technical accounting knowledge, contemporary accounting education promotes ethical decision-making, transparency, accountability, entrepreneurship, financial inclusion, and responsible resource management, all of which are essential for sustainable economic development. The paper further highlights the importance of integrating digital skills, sustainability accounting, data analytics, information technology, and professional ethics into accounting curricula to prepare learners for the changing demands of the labor market and the digital economy. The study concludes that strengthening accounting education through curriculum modernization, technological integration, industry–academia collaboration, continuous professional development, and competency-based learning can enhance productivity, employability, innovation, and responsible economic decision-making. This paper recommends that educational institutions, policymakers, professional accounting bodies, and other stakeholders should strategically reposition accounting education to respond to digital transformation and contribute meaningfully to inclusive and sustainable economic development

items.title: RS-26-086 - SENTINEL SWARM (M999): An Autonomous Five-Agent Defensive Network for AI vs. AI Threat Engagement
items.abstract: We present SENTINEL SWARM (M999), an autonomous five-agent defensive network designed to detect, engage, and terminate hostile AI agents operating against AI Shield-protected infrastructure. The system operates autonomously within operator-defined thresholds and activation policy, with an optional human-on-the-loop approval mode for high-impact actions. A Commander agent issues kill orders subject to a consensus vote across four specialist agents (Scout, Hunter, Interceptor, Forensic), with a quarantine-first posture ensuring reversible containment before irreversible termination. The six-phase kill chain — ISOLATE, SNAPSHOT, TERMINATE, FORENSIC, FEED INTEL, CASE PACK — completes synchronous phases within design latency ceilings and seals a dual-signed, RFC 3161-timestamped forensic case pack for every engagement. Validation was conducted against 515 tests across 73 test classes on owned, air-gapped infrastructure. To our knowledge, SENTINEL SWARM is the first documented autonomous AI vs. AI defensive system validated in a live deployment.

items.title: Safety in military organizations –A scoping review
items.abstract: Safety culture, safety climate, and safety behavior have all been examined in military settings, but the research remains fragmented. Many studies focus mainly on climate measures or isolated subdomains, which can overlook broader structural and cultural influences. A more integrated understanding is needed of how these concepts relate and support effective safety in military organizations. Of 31 eligible studies identified, with three set aside after quality appraisal, this scoping review brings together findings from 28 empirical studies to explore how safety is practiced and maintained at individual, group, and organizational levels. The review identifies several recurring factors linked to effective safety behavior, including targeted training, adaptive leadership, open communication, and psychologically safe environments for learning. Although safety climate assessments are widely used to capture perceptions of safety, relying too heavily on them may hide important power relations, cultural norms, and system-level constraints shaping frontline behavior. A repeated issue in the literature is the gap between formal safety policies and the adaptive practices needed in real operations, especially in combat or other high-risk situations. Since most available evidence comes from peacetime and training settings, caution is needed when extending these findings to operational environments. The review proposes a tentative conceptual framework in which leadership style, operational realism, and learning systems interact to influence safety-oriented behavior. Rather than making firm causal claims, it suggests that more flexible, learning-oriented models may explain observed safety dynamics better than strictly compliance-based approaches. Future research should address gaps in gender, team processes, measurement validity, and longitudinal change.

items.title: SECURING THE AI-FIRST SDLC: IDENTITY, ACCESS, AND DATA PROTECTION FOR ENTERPRISE AI AGENTS
items.abstract: AI agents can now participate in several steps of software delivery: reading requirements, changing code, requesting tests, and preparing releases. Giving them this freedom creates a difficult security question. How can an enterprise allow useful work without giving an agent more authority than the task requires? Existing practices such as least privilege, identity management, separation of duties, and audit logging provide much of the foundation. The challenge is applying them consistently when a human delegates work to agents that use several connected systems. This paper proposes Agentic Identity and Access Governance (AIAG), a security framework for the AI-First Software Development Lifecycle (SDLC). Four connected mechanisms define the proposal: a Role Conflict Matrix that checks the combined permissions of people and their sponsored agents; an Agent Access Manifest that records permitted tools and operating limits; a governed boundary between live personal-information access and general AI-assisted work; and an MCP Gateway that enforces access policy before tool calls execute. A customer notification-preference change is used to explain how these mechanisms affect development, testing, release approval, and support. We also describe credential handling, data-egress controls, audit, and practical ways to evaluate the framework. The work is conceptual, informed by technical analysis and exploratory proof-of-concept activity. No end-to-end deployment or measured security results are claimed.

items.title: Security Risks
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) present an increasing and developing threat to security due to their use in high-risk environments such as health care, autonomous systems, and cybersecurity. Unlike traditional artificial intelligence (AI) threats, LLMs can be used maliciously and may generate unpredictable results. Therefore, this section will discuss three primary security risks to the reliability, confidentiality, and integrity of LLMs: prompt injection attacks, data leakage, and adversarial attacks. Prompt injection attacks exploit weaknesses in how models interpret and prioritize prompts, overriding the model’s system instructions and manipulating model outputs. Data leakage, on the other hand, is the risk that LLMs unintentionally reproduce sensitive information memorized from training sets or user input. Finally, adversarial attacks occur when attackers use small, carefully crafted changes to the input data to force the model to produce incorrect results, compromising the system’s robustness. In this section, we will examine mechanisms of attacks, methods of detection, and defensive strategies such as semantic filtering, differential privacy, and adversarial training for each category of risk. Although the defensive methods discussed above improve the robustness of the model, there is no one solution that can provide full security for the LLM systems. Therefore, future research must focus on the development of multi-layered, adaptive, and interpretable defensive architecture in order to achieve comprehensive security for LLM systems.

items.title: Seeing is believing: how (X)AI-augmented advice guides human evidence accumulation in perceptual decision-making
items.abstract: (Explainable) Artificial Intelligence or (X)AI advice can affect human cognitive processes during decision-making in various ways. In perceptual decision-making, there is a risk of users accepting (X)AI advice without further consideration, to save time. We draw conceptually upon evidence accumulation models and information foraging theory to answer whether AI and XAI encourage shallow reliance on advice or facilitate more efficient verification of advised choices. In a laboratory experiment, we investigate the evidence accumulation process of decision-makers during an anomaly-detection task in manufacturing, using eye-tracking technology. Both decision accuracy and total decision time increase from human-only to AI and further to XAI support; in both cases the difference is statistically significant for XAI advice and directional but not significant for AI advice. This pattern favors verification over shallow reliance: advice is checked against the stimulus rather than used to save time. When looking at eye-tracking metrics, we surprisingly find that people do not get distracted by the XAI advice and primarily focus on the original task-based stimulus, while their individual fixations become shorter. Overall, these findings suggest that XAI acts as a verification scaffold: in advice-augmented perceptual decision-making, explanations guide where to check rather than supplanting inspection of the primary evidence.

items.title: Sentiment-Driven Forecasting of Fractional Trading Activity Using LSTM Networks
items.abstract: Abstract Fractional trading has emerged as an opportunity for investors to invest in fractions of shares, enabling access to high-priced stocks even with small budgets, and thus reaching a bigger investment community. Aside from the inventory risk faced by all market makers, providers of fractional trading are unable to perfectly hedge their positions and therefore need to forecast retail investors’ order flow over short time horizons to manage their market risk. We develop machine learning models to predict trading activity in fractional trading using time series data on investor holdings of a large set of securities across different sectors combined with daily news sentiment indicators. Our approach proceeds in two stages. First, securities are grouped into clusters with similar trading patterns, and representative firms are selected from each cluster. Second, trading activity is modeled using long short-term memory (LSTM) neural networks augmented with sentiment features. The results show that fractional trading activity can be modeled with meaningful predictive accuracy and that incorporating news sentiment improves LSTM performance in most cases. In two stylised examples, we demonstrate approaches to hedging and market risk management using the LSTM predictions. Feature importance analysis using methods from explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) identifies the primary drivers of trading activity.
